newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks gain by lunch, hopes on IMF.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks gain by lunch, hopes on IMF.

text.p: Thai stocks advanced by the lunch break on Monday on expectations that the government would accept IMF package aimed at rescuing Thailand's ailing economy, brokers said.

"Investors bought large capitalised stocks as the finance minister held a news conference on the progress of talks with the IMF officials on the agency's package of measures to heal Thailand's economy," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.
The composite SET index rose 6.55 points to 658.59 on 1.7 billion baht turnover by the lunch break.
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya told a news conference that economic ministers were discussing the overall framework of the rescue package.
He said no loan details had yet been worked out, but said he would seek cabinet approval for the basic framework of the IMF package on Tuesday.

Brokers said the buying also came as liquidity in the money market was high after exporters sold the U.S. unit as they expected positive results for the baht from the economic ministers' meeting on the IMF measures.

Several key sectors gained by the lunch break. The finance counter topped the active list in terms of value, rising 1.14 percent, followed by the banking counter. which gained 1.63 percent, and the communication sector, which rallied 3.11 percent.
Nava Finance was the most active stock, gaining 1.25 baht to 31.50. Thai Farmers Bank rose two to 117.
